Define M_a=N^(-1) sum_x sigma_(x,a), a=1,2,3. For each known coefficient/control history, take a Hamiltonian H_s=H_int,s+(1/2) Omega_s dot sum_x sigma_x, where [H_int,s,M_a]=0 for all a. This includes arbitrary weighted Heisenberg exchange on any finite graph. The graph and couplings can vary in time if this symmetry is maintained. There is no small-interaction assumption. Each site resets to tau_s=(I+u_s dot sigma)/2, |u_s|<=1, at the common rate gamma*kappa_s, with kappa_s>=kappa>0. Let R_(x,u) replace site x by tau_s after tracing out its old state. The unobserved fast generator is A_s rho=-i[H_s,rho]+gamma*kappa_s sum_x(R_(x,u_s)rho-rho). This is a supplied valid Lindblad/reset architecture. It does not derive these reservoirs or their quantitative calibration from a material Hamiltonian. Continuous slow CP channels J_e^s have specified classical mode targets and observed/coarse labels. Their effects are R_e^s=(J_e^s)^*I=a_e^s I+beta_e^s dot M, a_e^s>=|beta_e^s|, sum_e R_e^s<=b(t)I. All hidden mode-changing and hidden self-event channels are included in b. Their CP outputs can be arbitrarily correlated or entangled. They need not preserve the reference family below. Instrument effects at deterministic slots tau_j likewise have the form E_(j,e)^s=c_(j,e)^s I+d_(j,e)^s dot M, c_(j,e)^s>=|d_(j,e)^s|, sum_e c_(j,e)^s=1, sum_e d_(j,e)^s=0. Instrument choices and known fast controls can depend on the permitted past record; the slots themselves are fixed. Unobserved fast bath records are not supplied to the controller. The same initialized causal policy is used in every compared experiment, with controller memory charged separately. 2. Pauli commutation and the local reset formula give A_s^* M=Omega_s cross M+gamma*kappa_s(u_s I-M). For the homogeneous equation the propagator is W_s(t,v)=exp[-gamma int_v^t kappa_s(w)dw] O_s(t,v), where O_s is the time-ordered rotation from Omega_s. This holds for arbitrarily rapid known controls; no differentiation of a control is needed. For F=alpha I+beta dot M the exact full-system spectrum has extrema alpha+-|beta|. Different-site operators commute, and all-aligned product states attain both endpoints. Thus ||F||=|alpha|+|beta|, osc(F)=2|beta|. Propagation sends beta to W_s(t,v)^T beta. Consequently every norm-at-most-one affine collective effect obeys osc(U_(v,t)^(s,*) F)<=2 exp[-a(t-v)], a=gamma*kappa. (2.3) The estimate is independent of N and of the interaction graph. For |r|<1, this product is proportional to exp[atanh(|r|) (r/|r|) dot sum_x sigma_x]. It commutes with H_int. Pure endpoints follow by continuity. The common field rotates every factor and the sum of local resets differentiates this product exactly according to (2.2). Hence it is an actual fast solution. Initialize r_s(0)=m_s on occupied modes and assign valid initial vectors on all other modes. Every m_s lies in the Bloch ball. Hidden transitions are integrated in that belief; their realized path is not available to the controller. The banks receive no slow post-event or Bayes updates. The physical predictor has 3r+r-1=4r-1 real coordinates. For two modes this is seven. Time, coefficient-evaluation state, numerical precision and all controller memory are additional resources. Keeping a history-dependent controller outside these seven variables does not make that history free. 4. COMPLETE-RECORD GUARANTEE Let A(dt)=b(t)dt+(1/2)sum_j delta_(tau_j)(dt), D(ds)=(5/4)b(s)ds+sum_j delta_(tau_j)(ds). (4.2) As usual a complete-record TV bound epsilon implies average conditional future-record error at most 2epsilon, averaged under the actual past-record law at a deterministic current time. It does not give uniformly accurate inference after every rare record. Two different spin systems have the SAME small reference law if they share the initialized causal policy, mode labels/prior, all initial bank vectors, fast vector coefficients, effect coefficients, target/coarse maps and slot schedule. Their permitted-record TV is at most the sum of their two bounds. They may have different N, different SU(2)-invariant interaction graphs, different higher initial correlations and different CP output maps. Each must independently satisfy its own physical and access assumptions. This is a scoped operational universality statement about the stated record. 5. A site identity retained by an environment and reused later is additional memory and is not equivalent to fresh sampling. The 1/N coefficient divides total sensing activity among sites. Random-site access, sensor availability and calibration have not been experimentally acquired by writing this CP formula. 6. Every K_x commutes with M_z, so for every polynomial f, J^*f(M_z)=f(M_z)(aI+bM_z). Successive count-word effects therefore contain (aI+bM_z)^k. It is generated by the collective spin components, so a Hamiltonian commuting with those components commutes with this entire algebra, even if its interaction graph is not permutation symmetric. INTERACTING QUANTUM SPINS: A SMALL POSITIVE LAW FOR THE PERMITTED RECORD
Private P1 construction, 2026-10-24. Version 1 after scoped native checks.

This note combines the separately proved quantum partial-memory theorem with
an explicit interacting spin module. It preserves every initial joint state;
the conclusion that only certain initial moments matter is proved for the
declared record and access budget. It is not an assumption of a product prior.
No historical priority, acquired apparatus or practical speedup is claimed.

1. THE SUPPLIED PHYSICAL FAMILY

There are N qubits and a classical hidden mode s in a set of size r. Within
each mode the initial quantum state mu_s is arbitrary, including entangled
and spatially inhomogeneous states. There are no coherent superpositions
between the classical mode labels. Define
  M_a=N^(-1) sum_x sigma_(x,a),       a=1,2,3.

For each known coefficient/control history, take a Hamiltonian
  H_s=H_int,s+(1/2) Omega_s dot sum_x sigma_x,
where [H_int,s,M_a]=0 for all a. This includes arbitrary weighted Heisenberg
exchange on any finite graph. The graph and couplings can vary in time if
this symmetry is maintained. There is no small-interaction assumption.

Each site resets to tau_s=(I+u_s dot sigma)/2, |u_s|<=1, at the common rate
gamma*kappa_s, with kappa_s>=kappa>0. Let R_(x,u) replace site x by tau_s
after tracing out its old state. The unobserved fast generator is
  A_s rho=-i[H_s,rho]+gamma*kappa_s sum_x(R_(x,u_s)rho-rho).
This is a supplied valid Lindblad/reset architecture. It does not derive
these reservoirs or their quantitative calibration from a material Hamiltonian.

Continuous slow CP channels J_e^s have specified classical mode targets and
observed/coarse labels. Their effects are
  R_e^s=(J_e^s)^*I=a_e^s I+beta_e^s dot M,
  a_e^s>=|beta_e^s|,       sum_e R_e^s<=b(t)I.
All hidden mode-changing and hidden self-event channels are included in b.
Their CP outputs can be arbitrarily correlated or entangled. They need not
preserve the reference family below. Instrument effects at deterministic
slots tau_j likewise have the form
  E_(j,e)^s=c_(j,e)^s I+d_(j,e)^s dot M,
  c_(j,e)^s>=|d_(j,e)^s|, sum_e c_(j,e)^s=1, sum_e d_(j,e)^s=0.
Instrument choices and known fast controls can depend on the permitted past
record; the slots themselves are fixed. Unobserved fast bath records are
not supplied to the controller. The same initialized causal policy is used
in every compared experiment, with controller memory charged separately.

2. EXACT FAST CLOSURE, POSITIVITY AND RELAXATION

Commutation with H_int removes its contribution to the collective vector.
Pauli commutation and the local reset formula give
  A_s^* M=Omega_s cross M+gamma*kappa_s(u_s I-M).           (2.1)
The retained reference vector for each mode therefore solves
  r_s'=Omega_s cross r_s+gamma*kappa_s(u_s-r_s).            (2.2)
The unit ball is preserved: on |r|=1 its radial derivative is at most zero.
For the homogeneous equation the propagator is
  W_s(t,v)=exp[-gamma int_v^t kappa_s(w)dw] O_s(t,v),
where O_s is the time-ordered rotation from Omega_s. This holds for arbitrarily
rapid known controls; no differentiation of a control is needed.

For F=alpha I+beta dot M the exact full-system spectrum has extrema
alpha+-|beta|. Different-site operators commute, and all-aligned product
states attain both endpoints. Thus
  ||F||=|alpha|+|beta|,      osc(F)=2|beta|.
Propagation sends beta to W_s(t,v)^T beta. Consequently every norm-at-most-one
affine collective effect obeys
  osc(U_(v,t)^(s,*) F)<=2 exp[-a(t-v)],       a=gamma*kappa. (2.3)
The estimate is independent of N and of the interaction graph. It does not
claim contraction of every microscopic observable.

There is an explicit positive realization of every bank, not just formally
feasible moments:
  sigma_s=rho(r_s)^(tensor N),      rho(r)=(I+r dot sigma)/2.
For |r|<1, this product is proportional to
exp[atanh(|r|) (r/|r|) dot sum_x sigma_x]. It commutes with H_int. Pure
endpoints follow by continuity. The common field rotates every factor and
the sum of local resets differentiates this product exactly according to
(2.2). Hence it is an actual fast solution. The true preparation and the
true post-event states are not asserted to be products or close to it.

3. CURRENT PREDICTIVE STATE AND INITIAL INFORMATION

Supply the initial mode prior p_s and conditional collective means
  m_s=Tr(mu_s M).
Initialize r_s(0)=m_s on occupied modes and assign valid initial vectors on
all other modes. Every m_s lies in the Bloch ball. Every fast-propagated
admitted effect remains affine in I,M, so its expectation in mu_s equals
its expectation in rho(m_s)^(tensor N) exactly. Thus the initial tested
error beta_0 in the general theorem is ZERO, however different their
entanglement, pair correlations or spatial structure may be.

Effective rates and slot probabilities are
  qbar_e^s=a_e^s+beta_e^s dot r_s,
  Pbar_(j,e)^s=c_(j,e)^s+d_(j,e)^s dot r_s.
They are positive and obey the required total budgets. Evolve the exact
classical mode belief p_hat by the finite-state count filter and slot
updates of QUANTUM_PARTIAL_MEMORY_AND_ORDERED_ACCESS_V1.txt. Hidden transitions
are integrated in that belief; their realized path is not available to the
controller. The banks receive no slow post-event or Bayes updates.

The physical predictor has 3r+r-1=4r-1 real coordinates. For two modes this
is seven. Time, coefficient-evaluation state, numerical precision and all
controller memory are additional resources. Keeping a history-dependent
controller outside these seven variables does not make that history free.

4. COMPLETE-RECORD GUARANTEE

Let
  A(dt)=b(t)dt+(1/2)sum_j delta_(tau_j)(dt),
  D(ds)=(5/4)b(s)ds+sum_j delta_(tau_j)(ds).
The general theorem with (2.3) and beta_0=0 proves
  TV(P_Y,Pbar_Y)<=min{1, int_(s<t) 2exp[-a(t-s)] D(ds)A(dt)}. (4.1)
The record includes the entire permitted measurement and feedback history,
not just its means or single-time statistics. With no fixed slots and b<=B,
  TV<=min{1, (5B^2/(2a))[T-(1-exp(-aT))/a]}.                (4.2)
As usual a complete-record TV bound epsilon implies average conditional
future-record error at most 2epsilon, averaged under the actual past-record
law at a deterministic current time. It does not give uniformly accurate
inference after every rare record.

Two different spin systems have the SAME small reference law if they share
the initialized causal policy, mode labels/prior, all initial bank vectors,
fast vector coefficients, effect coefficients, target/coarse maps and slot
schedule. Their permitted-record TV is at most the sum of their two bounds.
They may have different N, different SU(2)-invariant interaction graphs,
different higher initial correlations and different CP output maps. Each
must independently satisfy its own physical and access assumptions. This
is a scoped operational universality statement about the stated record.

5. A DERIVED LOCAL INSTRUMENT INTERFACE

For an effect aI+beta dot M with a>=|beta|, set
  K_x=sqrt(aI+beta dot sigma_x),
  J(rho)=N^(-1) sum_x K_x rho K_x^dagger.
Then J is CP and J^*I=aI+beta dot M exactly. For discrete instruments take
the analogous square roots for each (c_e,d_e); their summed map is TP.
This supplies compatible physical quantum maps including their backaction.

This construction coarsens a fresh site choice with uniform weight before
outcome conditioning. The site posterior after a continuous count is generally
intensity biased. A reported site gives individual effects sigma_x, outside the small
collective module. A site identity retained by an environment and reused
later is additional memory and is not equivalent to fresh sampling.
The 1/N coefficient divides total sensing activity among sites. Fixed-rate
detection at every site instead makes B grow with N; (4.2) charges that
increase. Random-site access, sensor availability and calibration have not
been experimentally acquired by writing this CP formula.

6. EXACT FILTERS AND FAILURE OUTSIDE THE MENU

Even the local coarsened instrument generally requires higher moments in an
EXACT conditional filter. Take beta=b e_z and a>|b|>0. Every K_x commutes
with M_z, so for every polynomial f,
  J^*f(M_z)=f(M_z)(aI+bM_z).
Successive count-word effects therefore contain (aI+bM_z)^k. Since M_z has
N+1 distinct eigenvalues, the first N+1 powers are linearly independent.
Strictly ordered event-time densities tend to these products as successive
gaps tend to zero; simultaneous physical counts are not assumed. Thus an
exact unnormalized LINEAR predictive space valid for all preparations has
dimension at least N+1 for this menu. This is not a fixed-error or nonlinear
memory lower bound. The approximate seven-variable law avoids resolving
such high-order rare-event distinctions under its finite access budget.

The strongest exact baseline must still be retained. For the explicit
permutation-covariant coarsened instruments, identical resets and global
fields, the algebra of permutation-invariant operators is preserved.
It is generated by the collective spin components, so a Hamiltonian
commuting with those components commutes with this entire algebra, even
if its interaction graph is not permutation symmetric. Its dimension is
binomial(N+3,3)=sum_j(2j+1)^2=O(N^3). A direct proof groups the Pauli-string
basis into site-permutation orbits indexed by the four counts of I,X,Y,Z.
Their disjoint orbit sums are independent. Products of collective components
generate these orbit sums by induction on distinct-site degree; coincident-site
terms reduce to lower degree by Pauli multiplication. Identical local
superoperators change one of the four counts and act polynomially on this
basis. Consequently an exact
symmetry-reduced filter can be polynomial here. A comparison of seven
variables against a mandatory 4^N density matrix would be misleading.
Arbitrary additional CP outputs need not preserve this exact symmetry
baseline, but remain covered by (4.1) if the stipulated effect contract holds.

A two-spin singlet and I/4 both have collective mean zero. A singlet
projector gives probabilities one and one-quarter. Its effect is outside
span{I,M_x,M_y,M_z}. The difference is not bounded by (4.1) unless that new
effect is included and its appropriate relaxation certificate supplied.
Exchange energy and spatial pair correlations are likewise outside this
particular readout contract. This theorem is not a general thermodynamic,
energy-transport or local hydrodynamic law for interacting matter.

7. PRECISION, ACQUISITION AND EVOLUTION WORK

Initial mean error |m_s-r_s(0)|<=delta gives
  beta_0(t)<=delta exp(-at).
For an absolutely continuous numerical vector in the Bloch ball, let its
residual against the SAME known fast coefficients be
  xi_s(t)=rtilde_s'(t)-Omega_s cross rtilde_s(t)
                         -gamma*kappa_s(u_s-rtilde_s(t)).
If |xi_s(t)|<=rho(t) uniformly over modes and all admitted common record
histories, variation of constants gives
  |r_s(t)-rtilde_s(t)|<=delta exp(-at)
                         +int_0^t exp[-a(t-v)]rho(v)dv.    (7.1)
The same expression bounds all normalized signed-effect errors. Integrating
it against A(dt) gives the additional bank-computation allowance. Candidate
vectors must remain physical; positivity is part of this certificate.
The initial delta contribution is charged ONCE: either through beta_0, or
through the complete allowance (7.1). Numerical jumps or projections require
separate residual atoms; absolute continuity is the stated contract. A random
residual allowance must remain inside expectation under the justified
comparison marginal. Mode-filter, event-sampler and controller errors require
their own conditional kernel certificate and are not covered by (7.1).

For a piecewise constant coefficient segment the affine three-dimensional
flow can be propagated using a constant-size matrix exponential per mode;
it need not step through N*gamma microscopic reset events. Every actual
coefficient segment and the chosen exponential precision still costs work.
Arbitrarily rapid input changes are permitted mathematically, not processed
for free. With sparse channel targets, constructing rates and filter updates
costs the actual mode/channel enumeration; dense mode mixing costs r^2.

The theorem proves which initial moments suffice, but does not obtain the
conditional means of rare hidden modes from a passive experiment, identify
the retained modes, or learn the controlled kinetic functions. In particular
energy ratios alone do not determine these functions. These are supplied
or separately acquired physical inputs.

The intensive M is not the N20 critical scaled spin. Its critical scaling,
nonlinear readouts, symmetry-breaking interactions and nonuniform reset
architectures require a new invariant module or a tested residual. Existing
Green, critical-spin, measurement and memory results remain unchanged.

The general theorem and its two scoped independent native checks are held
separately. The spin algebra, positive-product realization and local Kraus
interface were independently derived in
agents/conditional_memory_construction_20261024/
INTERACTING_QUANTUM_VECTOR_MODE_COROLLARY.txt,
SHA256 6f6ba43fec6ec04f6ab9c13603d5f47bb678cbeab4659052eb574856b9bfd02a.
Its exact two-qubit diagnostic checks supplement, rather than replace, the
arbitrary-N proof. The root additions were checked in

SHA256 81a3f6dfd9a34aaf17188f560fa8ab353df1742e768f63ca73ea02f28e132af6.

  c_(j,e)^s>=|d_(j,e)^s|, sum_e c_(j,e)^s=1, sum_e d_(j,e)^s=0.
Instrument choices and known fast controls can depend on the permitted past
record; the slots themselves are fixed. Unobserved fast bath records are
not supplied to the controller. The same initialized causal policy is used
in every compared experiment, with controller memory charged separately.

2. EXACT FAST CLOSURE, POSITIVITY AND RELAXATION

Commutation with H_int removes its contribution to the collective vector.
Pauli commutation and the local reset formula give
  A_s^* M=Omega_s cross M+gamma*kappa_s(u_s I-M).           (2.1)
The retained reference vector for each mode therefore solves
  r_s'=Omega_s cross r_s+gamma*kappa_s(u_s-r_s).            (2.2)
The unit ball is preserved: on |r|=1 its radial derivative is at most zero.
For the homogeneous equation the propagator is
  W_s(t,v)=exp[-gamma int_v^t kappa_s(w)dw] O_s(t,v),
where O_s is the time-ordered rotation from Omega_s. This holds for arbitrarily
rapid known controls; no differentiation of a control is needed.

For F=alpha I+beta dot M the exact full-system spectrum has extrema
alpha+-|beta|. Different-site operators commute, and all-aligned product
states attain both endpoints. Thus
  ||F||=|alpha|+|beta|,      osc(F)=2|beta|.
Propagation sends beta to W_s(t,v)^T beta. Consequently every norm-at-most-one
affine collective effect obeys
  osc(U_(v,t)^(s,*) F)<=2 exp[-a(t-v)],       a=gamma*kappa. (2.3)
The estimate is independent of N and of the interaction graph. It does not
claim contraction of every microscopic observable.

There is an explicit positive realization of every bank, not just formally
feasible moments:
  sigma_s=rho(r_s)^(tensor N),      rho(r)=(I+r dot sigma)/2.
For |r|<1, this product is proportional to
exp[atanh(|r|) (r/|r|) dot sum_x sigma_x]. It commutes with H_int. Pure
endpoints follow by continuity. The common field rotates every factor and
the sum of local resets differentiates this product exactly according to
(2.2). Hence it is an actual fast solution. The true preparation and the
true post-event states are not asserted to be products or close to it.

3. CURRENT PREDICTIVE STATE AND INITIAL INFORMATION

Supply the initial mode prior p_s and conditional collective means
  m_s=Tr(mu_s M).
Initialize r_s(0)=m_s on occupied modes and assign valid initial vectors on
all other modes. Every m_s lies in the Bloch ball. Every fast-propagated
admitted effect remains affine in I,M, so its expectation in mu_s equals
its expectation in rho(m_s)^(tensor N) exactly. Thus the initial tested
error beta_0 in the general theorem is ZERO, however different their
entanglement, pair correlations or spatial structure may be.

Effective rates and slot probabilities are
  qbar_e^s=a_e^s+beta_e^s dot r_s,
  Pbar_(j,e)^s=c_(j,e)^s+d_(j,e)^s dot r_s.
They are positive and obey the required total budgets. Evolve the exact
classical mode belief p_hat by the finite-state count filter and slot
updates of QUANTUM_PARTIAL_MEMORY_AND_ORDERED_ACCESS_V1.txt. Hidden transitions
are integrated in that belief; their realized path is not available to the
controller. The banks receive no slow post-event or Bayes updates.

The physical predictor has 3r+r-1=4r-1 real coordinates. For two modes this
is seven. Time, coefficient-evaluation state, numerical precision and all
controller memory are additional resources. Keeping a history-dependent
controller outside these seven variables does not make that history free.

4. COMPLETE-RECORD GUARANTEE

Let
  A(dt)=b(t)dt+(1/2)sum_j delta_(tau_j)(dt),
  D(ds)=(5/4)b(s)ds+sum_j delta_(tau_j)(ds).
The general theorem with (2.3) and beta_0=0 proves
  TV(P_Y,Pbar_Y)<=min{1, int_(s<t) 2exp[-a(t-s)] D(ds)A(dt)}. (4.1)
The record includes the entire permitted measurement and feedback history,
not just its means or single-time statistics. With no fixed slots and b<=B,
  TV<=min{1, (5B^2/(2a))[T-(1-exp(-aT))/a]}.                (4.2)
As usual a complete-record TV bound epsilon implies average conditional
future-record error at most 2epsilon, averaged under the actual past-record
law at a deterministic current time. It does not give uniformly accurate
inference after every rare record.

Two different spin systems have the SAME small reference law if they share
the initialized causal policy, mode labels/prior, all initial bank vectors,
fast vector coefficients, effect coefficients, target/coarse maps and slot
schedule. Their permitted-record TV is at most the sum of their two bounds.
They may have different N, different SU(2)-invariant interaction graphs,
different higher initial correlations and different CP output maps. Each
must independently satisfy its own physical and access assumptions. This
is a scoped operational universality statement about the stated record.

5. A DERIVED LOCAL INSTRUMENT INTERFACE

For an effect aI+beta dot M with a>=|beta|, set
  K_x=sqrt(aI+beta dot sigma_x),
  J(rho)=N^(-1) sum_x K_x rho K_x^dagger.
Then J is CP and J^*I=aI+beta dot M exactly. For discrete instruments take
the analogous square roots for each (c_e,d_e); their summed map is TP.
This supplies compatible physical quantum maps including their backaction.

This construction coarsens a fresh site choice with uniform weight before
outcome conditioning. The site posterior after a continuous count is generally
intensity biased. A reported site gives individual effects sigma_x, outside the small
collective module. A site identity retained by an environment and reused
later is additional memory and is not equivalent to fresh sampling.
The 1/N coefficient divides total sensing activity among sites. Fixed-rate
detection at every site instead makes B grow with N; (4.2) charges that
increase. Random-site access, sensor availability and calibration have not
been experimentally acquired by writing this CP formula.

6. EXACT FILTERS AND FAILURE OUTSIDE THE MENU

Even the local coarsened instrument generally requires higher moments in an
EXACT conditional filter. Take beta=b e_z and a>|b|>0. Every K_x commutes
with M_z, so for every polynomial f,
  J^*f(M_z)=f(M_z)(aI+bM_z).
Successive count-word effects therefore contain (aI+bM_z)^k. Since M_z has
N+1 distinct eigenvalues, the first N+1 powers are linearly independent.
Strictly ordered event-time densities tend to these products as successive
gaps tend to zero; simultaneous physical counts are not assumed. Thus an
exact unnormalized LINEAR predictive space valid for all preparations has
dimension at least N+1 for this menu. This is not a fixed-error or nonlinear
memory lower bound. The approximate seven-variable law avoids resolving
such high-order rare-event distinctions under its finite access budget.

The strongest exact baseline must still be retained. For the explicit
permutation-covariant coarsened instruments, identical resets and global
fields, the algebra of permutation-invariant operators is preserved.
It is generated by the collective spin components, so a Hamiltonian
commuting with those components commutes with this entire algebra, even
if its interaction graph is not permutation symmetric. Its dimension is
binomial(N+3,3)=sum_j(2j+1)^2=O(N^3). A direct proof groups the Pauli-string
basis into site-permutation orbits indexed by the four counts of I,X,Y,Z.
Their disjoint orbit sums are independent. Products of collective components
generate these orbit sums by induction on distinct-site degree; coincident-site
terms reduce to lower degree by Pauli multiplication. Identical local
superoperators change one of the four counts and act polynomially on this
basis. Consequently an exact
symmetry-reduced filter can be polynomial here. A comparison of seven
variables against a mandatory 4^N density matrix would be misleading.
Arbitrary additional CP outputs need not preserve this exact symmetry
baseline, but remain covered by (4.1) if the stipulated effect contract holds.

A two-spin singlet and I/4 both have collective mean zero. A singlet
projector gives probabilities one and one-quarter. Its effect is outside
span{I,M_x,M_y,M_z}. The difference is not bounded by (4.1) unless that new
effect is included and its appropriate relaxation certificate supplied.
Exchange energy and spatial pair correlations are likewise outside this
particular readout contract. This theorem is not a general thermodynamic,
energy-transport or local hydrodynamic law for interacting matter.

7. PRECISION, ACQUISITION AND EVOLUTION WORK

Initial mean error |m_s-r_s(0)|<=delta gives
  beta_0(t)<=delta exp(-at).
For an absolutely continuous numerical vector in the Bloch ball, let its
residual against the SAME known fast coefficients be
  xi_s(t)=rtilde_s'(t)-Omega_s cross rtilde_s(t)
                         -gamma*kappa_s(u_s-rtilde_s(t)).
If |xi_s(t)|<=rho(t) uniformly over modes and all admitted common record
histories, variation of constants gives
  |r_s(t)-rtilde_s(t)|<=delta exp(-at)
                         +int_0^t exp[-a(t-v)]rho(v)dv.    (7.1)
The same expression bounds all normalized signed-effect errors. Integrating
it against A(dt) gives the additional bank-computation allowance. Candidate
vectors must remain physical; positivity is part of this certificate.
The initial delta contribution is charged ONCE: either through beta_0, or
through the complete allowance (7.1). Numerical jumps or projections require
separate residual atoms; absolute continuity is the stated contract. A random
residual allowance must remain inside expectation under the justified
comparison marginal. Mode-filter, event-sampler and controller errors require
their own conditional kernel certificate and are not covered by (7.1).

For a piecewise constant coefficient segment the affine three-dimensional
flow can be propagated using a constant-size matrix exponential per mode;
it need not step through N*gamma microscopic reset events. Every actual
coefficient segment and the chosen exponential precision still costs work.
Arbitrarily rapid input changes are permitted mathematically, not processed
for free. With sparse channel targets, constructing rates and filter updates
costs the actual mode/channel enumeration; dense mode mixing costs r^2.

The theorem proves which initial moments suffice, but does not obtain the
conditional means of rare hidden modes from a passive experiment, identify
the retained modes, or learn the controlled kinetic functions. In particular
energy ratios alone do not determine these functions. These are supplied
or separately acquired physical inputs.

The intensive M is not the N20 critical scaled spin. Its critical scaling,
nonlinear readouts, symmetry-breaking interactions and nonuniform reset
architectures require a new invariant module or a tested residual. Existing
Green, critical-spin, measurement and memory results remain unchanged.
